node.title: Re^4: Can't exec "command": No such file or directory error
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
What's weird is if I do command task on alpine directly on the command line, it runs just fine. It's only with perl I seem to have the problem.

What you type at the command line gets interpreted by whatever shell you have running at that moment. The shell may recognise built-in commands that don't exist as binaries in the filesystem. In some cases, commands can be both built-ins and exist as binaries in the file system, with (AFAIK) the built-ins taking precedence over the binaries in the PATH (again, I'm only talking about commands typed into the shell here). For example, when you type echo in [man://bash], the shell will use its built-in instead of calling /bin/echo. You can get the binary if you explicitly run /bin/echo.

But if you explicitly want to access the shell built-in from Perl, the tricky thing is that Perl's [doc://system] and similar functions may or may not run the command in a shell ([id://1205217|/bin/sh!]) for you depending on what arguments you give them. So, you'll need to be explicit about calling the shell, and the form I [id://11148870|showed] will prevent Perl from running a shell implicitly, and then we explicitly run [man://zsh] and give it a command to execute with -c, as if typed into the shell.

There is also a bit more about this in my node [id://1180578].

A few edits for clarity.
